newsitem.title: USA: Missouri restaurateurs simmer over safety report.
newsitem.headline: Missouri restaurateurs simmer over safety report.

text.p: Restaurateurs simmered Thursday after a report said food safety standards in this city were among the worst in the United States.

The report, called "Dine at Your Own Risk," charged that Jackson County, Missouri, was among the most negligent in the nation when it came to applying recent standards recommended by the U.S. Food and Drug Administration.
The report was released Wednesday by the Centre for Science in the Public Interest, the same group that whipped up public concern over fat levels in popcorn and Chinese food.

"Local restaurateurs are outraged that somehow through innuendo and suggestion the restaurant industry in this area has been identified as under-regulated," said Carl Degen, executive director of the Missouri Restaurant Association.

Larry Morgan, an inspector for the Jackson County health department, said the report was misleading because it suggested restaurants were allowed to violate basic rules governing cooking and refrigeration temperatures.

"They are required to follow (standards on) cooking and refrigeration temperatures. They're just not the newest ones," Morgan said. He explained that Jackson County followed statewide standards based on a 1976 FDA code.
Many states, including Missouri, have refused to adopt the more recent FDA code because of a variety of objections.
Other areas that ranked poorly in the survey were Dallas, Detroit, San Francisco and the counties of Jefferson, Kentucky, and Atlantic, New Jersey.
